To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein part of the PDNA building block contributes significantly to hydrodynamic behaviors but marginally affects hybridization properties.
protein domains covalently attached at the end of a nucleic acid chain do not significantly modify the nucleic acid properties and can be used to design hybrid structures with specific properties.

the self-assembly and dynamics of protein-DNA hybrids are governed by a delicate balance between the intrinsic properties of the nucleotide and protein components and the interplay between these components and the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of novel hybrid materials and their self-assembly properties in solution and on surface.
the development and characterization of new hybrid materials with potential applications in nanotechnology.
the design and characterization of synthetic proteo-DNA assemblies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDNAs are versatile building blocks for creating functional scaffolds with optical and/or electrical properties.
protein-DNA conjugates are able to self-assemble into large complexes with properties that are similar to regular DNA but also different.
protein-DNA hybrid molecules are able to self-assemble in solution to form large structures that can interact with surfaces or membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-assembly properties of PDNAs in solution and on solid surfaces are similar to those of regular DNA.
PDNA structures can be designed and prepared to be used as building blocks to construct functional scaffolds.
PDNA building blocks can self-assemble and associate with other biomolecules to form functional supramolecular architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein component of PDNA can be considered as a simple linker, with no significant influence on the nucleic domain properties.
the protein component in PDNAs does not interfere with DNA hybridization and can be used to control assembly size and surface properties.
the protein part does not interfere with DNA self-assembly but rather provides additional features to DNA structures.
